resources.string: Select a component to see its purpose and interactive preview.
Use the controls below to exercise the component.
A Material 3 page shell with a transparent floating title bar, protected blurred edges, safe content padding and an optional anchored floating action.
A transparent page and sheet bar with an optional independently centered single-line title, floating back and action buttons, adaptive overflow, and optional auto-hide with tap-to-reveal.
A lazy adaptive grid that chooses its column count from available width while applying shared spacing and safe content padding.
A centered, width-constrained, vertically scrollable detail layout that respects page and navigation insets.
A circular floating page action that uses Android Kit’s shared translucent surface treatment and touch target.
A single contract for loading, empty and error states, with optional supporting copy and a recovery action.
A titled, optionally described section whose content is grouped in a themed Material 3 card.
A two-column label and value row for concise details and formatted data.
A compact card that emphasizes one value beneath a descriptive label.
A labeled form section that groups related editor controls in a shared card.
An adaptive field pair that uses a row when space allows and stacks fields on narrower widths.
A full-row accessible switch with optional supporting text and state owned by the caller.
A read-only outlined field that behaves as a button for opening a caller-owned picker.
An inline editor for adding unique strings and removing existing values as input chips.
A Material 3 confirmation dialog with shared labels and caller-owned form content.
An accessible settings row with optional leading, supporting and trailing content.
A modal bottom sheet with optional title chrome, close or back actions, spacing and safe insets.
A circular add action with shared sizing, semantics and floating surface styling.
A floating horizontal container for compact action-bar items.
An icon-only action-bar item that keeps its label in accessibility semantics.
An action-bar item that presents an icon with a visible text label.
A compact text-only action-bar item for clear secondary or primary commands.
A More action that converts typed icon-and-label actions into a themed overflow menu.
The low-level themed popup container used by action and navigation flyouts, with arbitrary menu content.
An adaptive navigation shell that uses a floating compact menu on small windows and Material 3 navigation suites on larger ones.
Buttons keep their semantics while sharing shape, spacing and emphasis.
Loading, empty and error states use one composable contract.
Add an item or choose retry to exercise the action callback.
Open each page to test the real compact menu variation.
Each page uses its variation as the live page action.
Compact destinations show both their icons and labels.
Compact destinations keep labels in accessibility semantics while displaying icons only.
Switch destinations, open the overflow flyout, and scroll this page to verify that the menu remains anchored.
The primary action combines an icon with a visible label.
A compact group exposes icon actions with accessible descriptions.
Text actions provide a clear secondary and primary choice.
Additional content keeps the page meaningfully scrollable.
This section verifies that floating controls stay anchored while content continues beneath them.
Adaptive cards flow from one column to a wide grid.
List and detail become two panes when the window allows it.
Sections stay readable with a constrained content width.
The detail pane appears beside the list on larger windows.
This detail is a Navigation 3 scene. It is full-screen on compact windows and paired with the list on larger windows.
Spacing, shapes and maximum content widths come from the active theme definition.
Long content remains reachable without overlapping floating navigation or actions.
System semantics, scalable text and minimum touch targets remain intact.
The layout reacts to available space instead of checking for a specific device.
Each root retains its own Navigation 3 history while the detail scene adapts.
Field pairs adapt without device-specific branches.
Receive a gentle follow-up when work is incomplete.
Reusable list editing with duplicate protection.
Extra fields make the form long enough to verify focus-aware scrolling.
Address fields remain visible when the software keyboard opens.
State-driven switches keep the whole row interactive.
Receive occasional product and component updates.
Allow other catalog users to discover this example profile.
A multiline field exercises keyboard and bring-into-view behavior near the page end.
The demo keeps state in memory; consuming apps decide how and where to persist it.
Changing language uses the official per-app locale API.
Formatters receive a locale explicitly and never depend on process-global state.
Light and Dark belong to the library. Prism exists only in this demo.
A colorful app-defined theme that proves the public extension point.
All floating surfaces are white; opacity applies consistently to every one.
Official Material 3 sheet behavior with shared chrome and safe insets.
The caller owns visibility and content. Android Kit supplies the adaptive chrome, spacing and accessibility labels.
This nested state uses the sheet’s titleless back and close controls.
The catalog consumes the same public artifacts intended for external open-source apps.
Additional rows keep this settings page scrollable across window sizes.
